reasoning: Verified against test/test_ducklib.py at HEAD. The DB/connection/prepared/data_chunk teardown helpers do re-read the slot after destroy: test_disconnect asserts duckdb_connection[0] == 0 after duckdb_disconnect (line 97), test_duckdb_destroy_data_chunk asserts data_chunk[0] == 0 after duckdb_destroy_data_chunk (line 208), and aux_destroy_prepared's caller test_prepare_and_destroy asserts stmt[0] == 0 after duckdb_destroy_prepare (line 287). By contrast, aux_destroy_value (lines 1165-1170) builds a scratch buf, calls duckdb_destroy_value(buf.ctypes.data), and returns without ever re-reading buf[0]; grepping every call site of aux_destroy_value plus every direct duckdb_destroy_logical_type / duckdb_destroy_scalar_function / duckdb_destroy_aggregate_function call in the file (123 destroy-related lines total) turns up zero post-destroy slot re-checks anywhere in the value/logical-type/function test sections. The only alloc==free leak assertions in the suite (lines 3373-3374, 3388-3389, 3465-3466) use numba's rtsys.get_allocation_stats(), which tracks numba NRT allocations (Python-side MemInfo/structref bridge), not DuckDB's internal heap -- confirmed by their location inside the structref/UDAF bridge tests (aux_alloc_and_export/_release helpers), unrelated to duckdb_destroy_value/logical_type/scalar_function. DuckDB's C API destroy_* functions take a pointer-to-handle and, per the established and consistently-demonstrated pattern for every other handle family in this same suite (db, connection, prepared statement, data chunk), zero the handle after freeing; duckdb_destroy_value/duckdb_destroy_logical_type/duckdb_destroy_scalar_function/duckdb_destroy_aggregate_function follow the identical `void destroy(handle_t *)` C API shape (ducklib.py lines 163-166, 240, 258, 763-784, 1219-1222), so the same slot-zero check would be available and meaningful here too -- it is simply never exercised for value/logical-type/function handles despite there being on the order of ~150 tests in those sections (well over half the 134 total test functions in the file touch these three handle families). The finding accurately characterizes a real, verifiable gap: no test proves destroy actually runs or frees DuckDB-side memory for these handle families, only that create/use worked before destroy was called. Severity 'low' is appropriate: this is purely a test-coverage/verification gap (matches the file's own 'notes' summary conceding no library bug was found), not a functional defect in ducklib.py itself, and the impact (undetected DuckDB-side leak or silent no-op destroy) is real but bounded to test rigor rather than shipped behavior.
